title: 人生四大階段
transcript: Is the 100 points you're desperately chasing right now really what you want? Life has four necessary stages. I walked through them this way myself. The first stage: pure happiness. When I was young, I had nothing, but owning one point was one point of joy. Hiding under the piano playing house... ...getting dirty all over, yet laughing happier than anyone. The happiness of that time didn't need conditions. The second stage: desperate chasing. You start to compare, to calculate. Others have cars and you don't. Others fly business class and you fly economy. You work hard to reach that 100 points. It's like a treadmill. You run faster and faster, your heart rate gets higher and higher, but you look down and you're still in the same place. Because that belt is a speed set by others, not your own rhythm. Third, the peak of emptiness. The car is bought, the house is lived in, the bag is owned. But what you have isn't the happiness you imagined. Because that 100 points was never your standard, it was someone else's. I left my hometown and started from scratch without any customers, worked my way up to become one of the top 100 Porsche sales consultants in the world. One day, a customer chatted with me and suddenly asked, 'Taixin, you're already number one, do you feel happy?' I smiled at the time and said I was quite happy, but after getting back into the car, I thought for a long time because I couldn't answer. That moment felt like climbing a very high mountain. Reaching the peak and looking down, you realize the scenery is beautiful, but your heart knows this mountain was never the one you wanted to climb. You climbed it because others were climbing it, so you followed. Or was it because you yourself wanted to climb? Then came the fourth stage: awakening. You ask yourself, what am I living for? And this question will torment you for a long time, but it's this pain that will force you to find your own answer. When you find it, you'll return to the first stage, where one point of possession is one point of joy. No longer out of ignorance, but because you truly understand. What's the difference? Childhood happiness is instinct; happiness after awakening is a choice. Which stage are you at? Leave a comment and let me know. I am Taixin, leading you to understand human nature and close high-value deals.

title: 2024年1月16日
transcript: If a customer comes to you today and says, 'If you return the commission to me, I'll buy from you.' Would you return it? Okay, this problem. We naturally decide based on the market mechanism. Then we first have to see, under this company system, can I return the commission? We don't do things that violate company policy. But if it is returnable, I believe 99% of sales professionals would return it just to close the deal. Right. When you have closed the deal for the sake of the return commission... I think... a return, it must be returned. But how to return it, and how to return it more comfortably than others? This means I can return it, but I can't return as much as others. I still make money because everything I do is meant to stabilize my price. So I will tell the customer a very classic line, everyone here can learn it. 'If you buy from me today, you won't find the cheapest price in Taiwan, but you won't find the most expensive either. I can only guarantee that after you walk out this door, you won't find a better sales consultant.' If I am 10,000 dollars different from others, but you get 10 years of service in exchange, do you think it's worth it? Let you decide. I should be moved to tears! Right! [audience laughter and applause]

title: 這是你想要的公司嗎？
transcript: Last year, our designer Yunpin, he told me during a meeting, 'Boss, wait a second, I have something to tell you.' I said, 'What is it? Say it.' He said, 'Boss, I want to go abroad for two and a half months.' Eh? Sounds a bit weird, right? You've been with the company for less than a year, and you want to go abroad for two and a half months. Suddenly I thought of something. When I was a salesperson before, I didn't dare to ask my supervisor for leave at all. So I felt envious in my heart and said, 'Fortunately, I'm your boss!' I just said, 'Okay, go ahead. Do you have money?' He said, 'No, I'm traveling on a budget.' Hmm? Budget travel? I don't think that's right either. Well, let me think of a way for you. Why don't you go abroad and play, and I'll still pay you your salary as you work. At least you'll have money to live abroad. What I want to cultivate in you is the ability to work in various places. What I want to cultivate is your ability to work for a lifetime, not just your ability to work at our EinFit. So I let him take his laptop and go to South America.

title: 你以為客戶要的是便宜？TikTok 2026 全球趨勢報告說
transcript: In 2026, TikTok published a global trend report. The conclusion is only one sentence: the era of impulsive consumption is over. Current customers, it's not that they don't buy things, they want to first understand one thing: why is this thing worth me spending this money? Have you met this type of customer? Obviously, there is a demand, a budget, and they also like the product, but they just don't place an order. You think they are waiting for a discount? No, they are waiting for you to give them a reason why it's worthwhile. I once had a guest who chatted three times. Every question was asked. Finally, he told me, 'Tai Xin, I'm not unable to afford it, I just don't know why I should buy it.' This sentence woke me up. From that day on, I no longer communicated with clients about how good my products are or how strong the specifications are. I started asking one question: 'Sir, what do you most hope to solve? If solved, what would your life look like?' Let the customer describe that picture themselves. When he sees that picture, he's not buying a product; he's buying for a better version of himself. It's like a date. You won't like him just because he treated you to a cheap meal. You will like him because he makes you feel that the time spent with him is meaningful. Clients are not afraid of your trouble; they're afraid you're not worth it. Clients are not afraid of you showing up; they're afraid you just want to make a deal. I am Tai Xin, helping you understand human nature and close high-value deals. Want to learn more about this logic? Join the sales community to learn more. Link in my bio.

transcript: Why are you professional but have low income? Because you don't love sales. It took me 10 years to find the problem. Solving skills decide salary, but sales skills decide wealth height. I used to be an engineer and hated sales. Because I think they are oily and soulless. Until I saw top salespeople living easier and earning more. I realized we hate low-quality sales, not sales itself. Income equals solving problems times sales. Sales is an amplifier. IBM started a sales school. No sales, no matter how good the tech, the company fails. AI is great but can't replace trust and love connection. Sales is your professional moat. From engineer to top salesperson, it's about three steps. First: precise positioning. We use behavioral patterns to find talent frequency. Don't imitate others. Do yourself best. Second: rational sales. Rely on psychology and tools, not social drinking. Third: sales system. Turn sensibility to stories, rationality to process. Everyone sells—doctors, lawyers. What is the professionalism of sales? I also give you all a few words, okay? Professionalism is: Don't give up your thoughts because of any smearing. Don't change your tone because of any emotions. Don't shake your thinking because of any doubts. Don't affect your performance because of any anxiety. This is called professionalism. So when I have earned the customer's money, and the customer is impatient with me, is there anything wrong? I am very happy, because I earned his money, right? If you want to earn money from every customer, you have this mindset of service. So we must take the customer's money, then we must help him solve problems, and serve him enthusiastically. You absolutely cannot have earned the customer's money and still be complaining about the customer. That's not right, is it? Do you think that will help your performance? It won't.
